# dtcloud_storage_policies (Data Source)

Lists the storage policies available in the region.

`storage_policy` is required on every volume and has no default, so this is how to find the valid
values. The endpoint returns only the policies with a non-zero quota for the project, so what comes
back is what this project can actually create volumes on, not the whole platform catalogue.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "dtcloud_storage_policies" "available" {}

output "policy_names" {
  value = data.dtcloud_storage_policies.available.names
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `name` (String) Only return the policy with this exact name. Applied by the provider — the API has no filter.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.
- `names` (List of String) Just the policy names, for when all you need is to check one is available.
- `policies` (List of Object) Storage policies this project has quota for. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--policies))

<a id="nestedatt--policies"></a>
### Nested Schema for `policies`

Read-Only:

- `id` (String)
- `name` (String)

## Behaviour worth knowing

~> **Pass the `name`, not the `id`.** The volume details endpoint reports the policy by name, so a
volume created with an id reads back as a name and every later plan proposes a change that never
converges.

* **`name` is applied by the provider** and must match exactly.
